tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms/intent (agent won't start, gateway fails, returns nothing, which version is live) rather than internals, explicitly lists trigger contexts even when the user doesn't name the underlying domain terms (runtime roles, VPC endpoints, SCPs, OTLP, aliasing), and stays concise at a few sentences.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an agent will not start or cannot be invoked, when a gateway or action group fails, when an agent returns nothing or produces no traces, when it behaves differently in production than in test, or when someone asks which agent version is actually live, even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining generic AWS/ML concepts and goes straight into service-specific distinctions (AgentCore vs Classic), check-ids, and router logic the agent would not know without this skill.
tests.evidence: These are two different services with different resources and different checks, and the first thing to establish is which one the user is running.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed lookup data (check catalogs, metrics, API quirks) is kept in references/ files; the body only contains a compact router table and procedural steps referencing those files rather than embedding the detail.
tests.evidence: Every finding is grounded in the catalogs under `references/`: `checks-agentcore.md` ... and `checks-agents.md`

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All eight references/ files are linked via markdown links somewhere in the body (collection-reference.md, checks-agentcore.md, checks-agents.md, api-quirks.md, metrics-and-logs.md, related-skills.md, router-details.md, runtime-sessions.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Router table and procedure entries tie each reference link to a specific triggering condition (e.g., specific error symptoms), clearly indicating when to load.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ without traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/high-risk operations (permission checks, alias resolution, migration advisory) are given exact sequential steps, while report assembly and hypothesis framing leave room for judgment, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: Step 2: Simulate the runtime role with `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` for every action it exercises ... any required action `denied` is **LLM-AC-001 (CRITICAL)**.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where tools/approaches could vary (e.g., which API to check first), the skill designates a default 'first read' per scenario in the router table rather than presenting equal options.
tests.evidence: | AgentCore runtime will not start / cannot invoke | `ListAgentRuntimes` / `GetAgentRuntime` for status, version, role ARN | `references/checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001) |

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedures teach generalizable investigation approaches (resolve alias before concluding production, name throttling layer before recommending) rather than one-off declarations, while still allowing specific check-ids and templates.
tests.evidence: Step 2: Resolve each alias with `ListAgentAliases` / `GetAgentAlias` to the **version** it serves; treat that version — not the latest prepared DRAFT — as production behaviour (LLM-AGT-007).

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section plus Error Handling section documenting non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain (alias vs DRAFT, no-datapoints vs zero, permission namespace gaps).
tests.evidence: "GetAgent shows PREPARED, so that config is what production runs." An agent's live behaviour is its alias → version resolution, not the latest prepared DRAFT.

tests.evidence: `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md` — consolidated review output (scope, findings with check-ids and severities, remediation, disclosed gaps)

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to check its findings for evidence, correctness, masking, and completeness before presenting.
tests.evidence: A finding with no evidence, or one that leaks sensitive material, is worse than no finding. Before you present an agent/runtime review, re-check your own output against this list.
